description: Granting tax concessions for the importation of Milk fish, which is used as the bait fish for the Long Line Fishing Method
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-12-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Owners of Multiday fishing vessels use the long line fishing method to catch fish which belongs to Tuna species. Small fish such as squid, milkfish, sailfish, flying fish etc. are used as bait for the said purpose. As a method of sustainable consumption of fish resources, the fish harvested using the long line fishing method is of high quality and therefore commands a high price in the international market. About 2,200 multiday fishing vessels in the country use the long line fishing method, and about 8,000 metric tons of bait fish are annually required for the purpose. However, only about 4,000 metric tons of that amount can be supplied locally. Therefore, with the support of the private sector, it is planned to produce milkfish for bait locally in the future. Accordingly, taking into account the proposal made by the Minister of Fisheries, Aquatic and Ocean Resources regarding the provision of tax concession on the import of milkfish until such time the said local products could be used, the Cabinet decided to import the required milkfish through the registered fishing societies, and to introduce a special commodity levy of Rs.180/- per kilogram of imported milkfish instead of the currently implemented tariff system and to provide a tax concession of Rs.130/- from that tax to fishing societies importing milkfish, was approved by the Cabinet.
